hypothesis: The ordinary reduction controller snapshots every PE before the hold-release and bounded heap callbacks queued by the new thresholds execute. Moving the contribution behind exactly one normal-priority heap turn should give the controller fresher frontier state, reduce road rounds, and lower road solve time.
scope: One exclusive Delta CPU node, 16 processes x 7 workers, 112 workers total, +old-scheduler. Compare separately built immediate and post-work binaries plus a duplicate immediate control. Do not combine contribution placement with heap coalescing, a round delay, or other queue changes.

acceptance.road_time: The geometric mean over per-source medians, using the geometric mean of the two immediate copies as the reference, improves by at least 10%, and post-work is faster than each immediate copy on at least three of four road sources.
acceptance.road_work: The geometric mean edge-attempt ratio versus the duplicate-immediate reference is at most 1.10.
acceptance.mesh_regression: The worst per-source post-work slowdown versus the duplicate-immediate reference is no larger than the greater of 5% and the observed immediate/control timing floor.
acceptance.decision: Passing is a screen, not default adoption: rerun in a second allocation before promotion. Any failed gate rejects the mechanism without tuning on these held-out sources.

prediction: Post-work contribution reduces controller rounds enough to improve road time by at least 10% without more than 10% additional edge work, while mesh24 remains within the duplicate-control noise floor.
